title: The Show That Owned 2024's Group Chats Is Back — and This Time Shanvika Came for Power, Not Just Revenge.
excerpt: Thukra Ke Mera Pyaar Season 2 drops on JioHotstar this Friday, trading college heartbreak for politics, betrayal, and a heroine who's done playing nice. If you missed the original, you were the only one.
body:
If you spent any part of 2024 wondering why your WhatsApp groups had suddenly turned into a war room arguing over whether **Shanvika** should ever take **Kuldeep** back, you already know what's happening this Friday. And if you somehow missed it — congratulations on being the one person in the diaspora who didn't get the forward.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=3nElVHkpuKo</youtube>

**Thukra Ke Mera Pyaar**, the small-town love story that ambushed everyone by becoming one of streaming's loudest sleeper hits, returns for a second season on **JioHotstar on June 19**. Season one was a deceptively simple thing: a poor boy, a rich girl, caste and class lines drawn hard between them, and a heartbreak so cleanly delivered it launched a thousand reaction reels. It had no business being as addictive as it was. That was the trick. It looked like a soap and hit like a thriller.

Season two is not interested in being underestimated twice.

> "With Season 2, we wanted to take the story beyond romance and explore the emotional consequences of love, betrayal, ambition, and power. The new season is bigger, more intense, and packed with unexpected twists." — Shraddha Pasi Jairath, creator-director

Here's the shift, and it's a juicy one. **Sanchita Basu** returns as **Shanvika Chauhan**, except the wounded girl from season one is gone. In her place is a woman moving through the ruthless corridors of small-town politics, refusing to play by anyone's rules — even if it means rewriting what a relationship is supposed to mean. "Shanvika is at the heart of Kuldeep's story," Basu said, "and this season brings out her strength and resilience in ways that are both powerful and emotional." Translation: she's not waiting by the phone this time. She's running for office and settling scores.

Across from her, **Dhaval Thakur**'s **Kuldeep Kumar** is the more haunted figure — a man chewed up by guilt over the mistake that detonated everything, dragged back into a web of politics and unfinished feeling he can't outrun. "Kuldeep is a man of contradictions," Thakur said, "strong yet vulnerable, righteous yet flawed. It's not just about the battles he fights outside, but the ones within." It's the kind of brooding, self-loathing male lead that Indian audiences have an endless, helpless appetite for, and Thakur leans all the way in.

Add **Aniruddh Dave** as the rival Dushyant Singh — the man who poisoned the well between the lovers the first time around — and you have all the ingredients of a binge you'll resent yourself for finishing in one night.

What makes this one worth flagging beyond the usual OTT churn is *who* made it land in the first place. Season one didn't come pre-loaded with stars or a marketing blitz. It grew the way the best desi serials always have — through aunties, group chats, and the sheer momentum of people needing to know what happens next. That's a different kind of hit than a Netflix algorithm push. It's earned. Creator **Shraddha Pasi Jairath** clearly knows it, and her promise that this chapter is "darker" and built to "stay with viewers long after the credits roll" reads less like PR and more like a dare.

For the diaspora, the where-to-watch is refreshingly clean. **JioHotstar** carries the show, and with the platform's expanding international footprint, NRIs across the US, UK and Canada can stream it in Hindi from June 19 without the usual VPN gymnastics. It's the perfect weekend watch for the homesick — small-town India rendered in all its gossip, grudges, and grandeur, the kind of melodrama that tastes like home precisely because it's so gloriously over the top.

Season one made you fall for a love story. Season two is betting you'll stay for the bloodsport. Clear your Friday night — and maybe warn the group chat. They're about to get loud again.
